state_schema.coordinate_frame: Solar-system barycentric ICRF Cartesian state stored by the runner.
state_schema.matched_epoch_rule: Join state groups and progress rows by exact sample_index and exact float64 time_years=100*sample_index; no interpolation.
state_schema.numeric_serialization: Python csv.DictWriter applied str() to Python float values. Every relevant token must satisfy str(float(token)) == token, proving canonical shortest lossless float64 round-trip representation.
state_schema.decimal_construction: Construct Decimal directly from each original mass, position, velocity, time, and recorded-telemetry CSV token; never parse reference inputs through float.

energy_formulas.kinetic: K = sum_i 0.5*m_i*(vx_i^2+vy_i^2+vz_i^2), including the Sun and all ten real particles in the stored barycentric frame.
energy_formulas.newtonian_pair_potential: U_N = -G*sum_{i<j}(m_i*m_j/sqrt((x_j-x_i)^2+(y_j-y_i)^2+(z_j-z_i)^2)) over all 45 unordered real-particle pairs.
energy_formulas.initial_denominator: For each lane and numerical method independently, drift(t)=(E_corrected(t)-E_corrected(0))/abs(E_corrected(0)); use 1 J only if E_corrected(0)==0.

evaluation_methods.float64_matching: Independent implementation matching telemetry: numpy float64 kinetic array expression and np.sum; nested i then j Newtonian pair accumulation; body-index GR weighted-inverse-r2 accumulation; telemetry operation order for prefactor and corrected total.
evaluation_methods.compensated: Parse float64 inputs, explicitly enumerate kinetic component terms, 45 Newtonian pair terms, and 9 GR terms, combine each category and totals with Python math.fsum.
evaluation_methods.decimal_reference: Use decimal localcontext precision 60. Build all values and constants directly from CSV/manifest decimal strings. Perform squared norms, pair distances and Decimal.sqrt(), products, category sums, corrected totals, own-initial drift, statistics, and trend entirely in Decimal arithmetic.

statistics.maximum: max(abs(drift_t)) with earliest sample on ties; record value and epoch.
statistics.p99: Sort absolute drift values and select zero-based index 9900 because (N-1)*0.99=9900 exactly for N=10001; this equals numpy.percentile(...,99.0) linear behavior without interpolation.
statistics.fitted_trend: Unweighted OLS after centering times and drifts at their arithmetic means; report slope per year and slope*1000000 as fitted change over 1 Myr.
statistics.unchanged_trend_rule: abs(fitted_change_over_1myr) <= max(0.25*max_abs,1e-10) for every compared lane.
statistics.unchanged_monotonic_rule: The 0.25-day maximum, RMS, and p99 must each be <= the corresponding 0.5-day statistic; maximum nonmonotonicity is waived only if both maxima are <=1e-12.

numeric_tolerances.conditioning_overlap_rule: If the 0.5-to-0.25 difference in any decisive Decimal statistic is <= lane_worsening_significance_margin, that statistic cannot establish worsening.

classification_rules.BLOCKED: An input/provenance/schema/hash audit fails, required values are nonfinite, or float64 reconstruction does not reproduce recorded telemetry within the preregistered dynamic tolerances and the discrepancy is not identified.
classification_rules.ENERGY_TELEMETRY_PRECISION_LIMITED: Telemetry reconstruction passes; compensated and Decimal histories agree; the Decimal history removes 0.25-day worsening under all maximum/RMS/p99 rules and both Decimal lane trends satisfy the unchanged trend rule.
classification_rules.ENERGY_DRIFT_CONFIRMED: Telemetry reconstruction passes; compensated and Decimal histories agree within method_history_agreement_abs; Decimal and compensated maximum/RMS/p99 all show 0.25-day worsening over 0.5 day by more than lane_worsening_significance_margin; and the Decimal 0.25-day fitted-trend magnitude also exceeds the 0.5-day magnitude by more than that margin.
classification_rules.INCONCLUSIVE: Audits and telemetry reconstruction pass, but method disagreement, stored-state conditioning overlap, or mixed Decimal/compensated ordering prevents either precision-limited or confirmed-drift classification.
